svg.title: Painting on a mesh: from the brush to a texture file
svg.desc: In paint mode the left mouse button paints. The pointer ray finds the spot on the surface and its UV coordinates, the brush draws into a block of pixels kept in memory and shown live through a canvas texture, and at the end of each stroke the picture is saved as a PNG texture file in asset storage, which the object's material points to by id: one undo step per stroke.
svg.text: Painting on a mesh (texture painting, first slice)
Paint on surface, then drag the left mouse button over the object. Each stroke is one undo step.
1. The pointer finds a spot
three.js shoots a ray from the mouse
at the mesh and returns the UV
coordinate (u, v) of the hit: where
on the flat picture that spot lives.
No UV map: it says to Unwrap first.
2. The brush draws pixels
paintSegment (shared, tested) stamps
soft round dabs along the line from
the last touch, into a 1024 x 1024
block of RGBA bytes. A jump to
another piece of the map is not joined.
3. Shown live
Only the changed rectangle is copied
to a canvas; a CanvasTexture on the
object's material shows it at once.
The left button is the brush, so it
does not pan; right-drag still orbits.
4. End of the stroke: store it
The canvas becomes a PNG, its SHA-256 is the id,
the bytes go to asset storage, the scene gets a
"texture" record and material.colorMap = id.
Undo only changes that id (and the live picture
reloads). Saving packs the PNG; unused ones are dropped.
Not built yet
Layers, roughness and metalness painting, erase,
fill, mirror painting. (The GLB export carries the picture.)
Baking (normal, ambient occlusion and colour maps)
in a worker with a progress bar.
Painting on built-in shapes (they need Edit points first).
